entity_types.label: Competition
entity_types.description: A league, cup, tournament, series or fantasy league: the standing thing that runs year after year. Each edition of it is a season.

property_schema.description: One per competition, not per year. The sport pack says which values of sport and format apply. A fantasy league is a competition with level fantasy.

sport.description: Sport code from the sport pack, a machine name: american_football, basketball, baseball, ice_hockey, soccer (football/soccer), rugby, cricket, softball, volleyball, tennis, other. In conversation use the international name: American football, football (soccer), ice hockey.

level.description: Who plays in it. recreational covers adult rec and company leagues; fantasy is a fantasy league whose teams are rosters of real players.

format.description: league: table only. league_playoffs: regular season then a bracket. knockout: single or double elimination. group_knockout: groups then a bracket. series: best-of-N between two sides. round_robin: everyone plays everyone, no table beyond that. ladder: challenge-based ranking. exhibition: friendlies and showcases that enter no table.

match_format.description: The form of the game when the sport has several, in the sport pack's vocabulary: test, odi, t20 (cricket); 11v11, 7v7, futsal (football); union_15s, union_7s, league_13s (rugby); best_of_3, best_of_5, pro_set_8 (tennis); seven_inning (softball). The default for every match in the competition; an event's match_format overrides it.

governing_body.description: Who runs it: the national federation, the league office, the parks department, a friend group

region.description: Where it is based: a country, state, city or neighbourhood

website.description: Official site, league page or fantasy platform URL

scoring_system.description: Short label for how results turn into table points or wins, in the sport pack's vocabulary: 3-1-0, 2-1-0, 3-2-1-0, win_loss, sets_as_points, union_bonus_4try, league_2-1-0, ranking_points, ppr, half_ppr, standard, custom. Full detail in lore.

entity_types.label: Season
entity_types.description: One edition of a competition: the 2026 season of a pro league, Spring 2026 Co-ed Softball, the 2026-27 top flight, Week 1-17 of a fantasy league. Matches hang off seasons; standings are per season.

property_schema.description: Always PART_OF exactly one competition. Teams join it with COMPETES_IN. Standings are team stat_lines with scope season; the AI reads them, it never caches a table here.

label.description: The edition name as people say it: 2026, 2026-27, Spring 2026, Season 3

status.description: upcoming until the first match, active while matches are being played, completed once the final result is in, cancelled if abandoned

end_date.description: Last scheduled match or final, ISO 8601

stage.description: Where the season is right now, in the sport pack's stage vocabulary: preseason, regular_season, playoffs, group_stage, knockout, offseason

current_round.description: The round, week or matchday in progress: Week 9, Matchday 14, Round of 16

rounds_total.description: How many rounds, weeks or matchdays the regular season has

roster_deadline.description: ISO 8601 last day roster changes are allowed in this season: registration cut-off, transfer window close, trade deadline, roster freeze.

ruleset_notes.description: One line on anything unusual about this edition: shortened season, new playoff format, rule changes. Detail goes in lore.

entity_types.label: Team
entity_types.description: A side that competes: a club, franchise, national team, rec-league team, school team, or a fantasy roster. Rosters and staff attach to it; it enters seasons with COMPETES_IN.

property_schema.description: One entity per team for its whole life, across seasons. Season-specific things (division, seed, record) live on the COMPETES_IN edge and on season stat_lines, not here. A reserve, B or academy side is its own team, PART_OF the senior one.

team_type.description: club: a member-owned or independent club. franchise: a team in a closed pro league. national: a country's side. school: college or school. recreational: a rec, company or pub-league team. fantasy: a roster in a fantasy league. select: an all-star, travel or representative side. pair: two people who compete together as one side (a doubles pair, a beach volleyball pair); named after its players, and a new pairing is a new team.

status.description: active: competing or expected to. inactive: not entered this year but may return. defunct: gone. merged: folded into another team (link with PART_OF).

short_name.description: What people call it in conversation: the Rovers, the Mud Hens

abbreviation.description: Two to four letters as seen on a scoreboard: RIV, MUD

nickname.description: Mascot or nickname when it differs from the name: the Hens, the Blues

colors.description: Primary and secondary colors, e.g. red and gold

founded.description: Year founded, or when the rec team first got together

owner.description: Fantasy or franchise owner's display name when the owner is not tracked as a person entity

website.description: Team page, club site or fantasy team URL

entity_types.label: Person
entity_types.description: Anyone in the sport: a player, coach, manager, official, owner, commissioner, scout, analyst or fantasy manager. What they do for a team is on the PLAYS_FOR and STAFF_OF edges, so one person can be a player on one team and a coach of another.

property_schema.description: Keep this to sporting facts the owner gives you. Never record health details: no injuries, diagnoses, treatment or medical history. Availability (whether someone can play) is a status on their PLAYS_FOR edge, with no reason attached. For a minor, record first name and last initial only unless the owner asks for the full name, and nothing else personal.

primary_role.description: What they mostly are. coach includes head and assistant coaches; manager is the soccer-style boss or a rec-team organiser; executive covers owners, GMs, directors, commissioners; staff covers trainers, analysts, scouts, equipment; fantasy_manager runs a fantasy roster; fan is anyone tracked only as a supporter.

status.description: Career status. free_agent means not attached to any team right now.

birth_date.description: ISO 8601. Record only for adults and only when the owner gives it.

nationality.description: Country or countries they represent or are from

handedness.description: Sport-pack vocabulary: right, left, both, bats_right_throws_left, and so on

height_cm.description: Height in centimetres, for pro athletes only

weight_kg.description: Weight in kilograms, for pro athletes only

is_minor.description: true when the person is under 18. Triggers the minimal-data rules in rule/people_and_privacy.

external_id.description: An id on a stats site or fantasy platform, so the person can be matched to imports

entity_types.label: Event
entity_types.description: Anything that happens on a date: a match (the main case), plus drafts, trades, transfers, signings, practices, tryouts, awards nights and meetings. event_type says which. Matches carry scores and results; everything else carries its detail in lore.

property_schema.description: Named <Away> at <Home> — <YYYY-MM-DD> for matches (or <A> vs <B> at a neutral site). Every event carries date_year, date_month, date_day so the timeline tools can order it. A match is PART_OF its season, HELD_AT its venue, and has one COMPETED_IN edge per team. Scores live here and nowhere else.

event_type.description: match covers games, fixtures, ties, rubbers and fantasy matchups. transfer is a move between clubs for a fee or free; trade is a swap between teams in a closed league or a fantasy league; signing and release are one-team roster moves that change clubs; roster_move is a one-team move that changes a player's list or status without changing clubs (option, recall, activation, waiver claim, call-up, loan return). staff_change records a coach or manager arriving or leaving. bye is a scheduled round with no match for a team (INVOLVED_IN from the team, role subject); it never counts in standings unless the pack awards bye points.

status.description: postponed never started; keep the event and give it a new date when known. suspended started, was halted and resumes from the point of stoppage on a later date: keep the one event, date_* stay as day one, end_date is the day it finished. abandoned started but will not resume; result no_result unless the pack awards one, and a replay ordered from scratch is a new event with round Replay. forfeited: result awarded without play; the awarded score goes in the score fields and the reason in lore unless it is medical. rejected: a non-match event that was proposed and turned down (a vetoed trade, a lost waiver claim).

end_date.description: ISO 8601 last day for multi-day events: a Test match, a draft weekend, a tournament

timezone.description: IANA zone of the start time, e.g. America/New_York, when the world spans zones

stage.description: Sport-pack vocabulary: preseason, regular_season, wildcard, divisional, conference, final, group_stage, round_of_16, quarterfinal, semifinal, playoff, consolation, friendly, exhibition

round.description: Week, matchday, round or leg label inside the stage: Week 9, Matchday 14, Game 3, Leg 2

match_format.description: Overrides the competition's match_format for this event, in the pack's vocabulary (a seven-inning doubleheader game, a best-of-3 final in a best-of-5 tournament).

regulation_length.description: How long the match was scheduled to be when it differs from the sport's default, in the pack's units: 7 (innings), 20 (overs), 2x40 (minutes).

home_score.description: Final score of the home (or first-named) side, as a single number the sport pack defines: points, goals, runs, sets won (volleyball, tennis), rubbers won (a team tie). The headline number; periods holds the detail and score_display the human line.

away_score.description: Final score of the away (or second-named) side

periods.description: Ordered list of the scoring periods the match is made of, with keys the sport pack defines; every element carries number. Sets (volleyball, tennis): number, home, away, kind. Line scores (baseball, softball): number, home, away. Innings (cricket): number, batting_team, runs, wickets, balls, balls_allotted, all_out, declared, follow_on, target, kind. Quarters and periods when the owner wants them. home_score and away_score are the headline numbers this list is summarised into.

score_display.description: The score as a human would write it when numbers alone lose meaning: 287/6 (50 ov) v 251 (48.3 ov), 2-2 (4-3 pens), 27-24 OT

result.description: pending until completed. draw is a shared result in sports that have them; tie is a dead-level score in sports where that is rare and recorded separately (cricket, American football). Equal scores with decided_by regulation or extra_time are a draw; equal scores with decided_by penalties, shootout or super_over are a win for the side the pack names. no_result for abandoned or rained-off matches that count as neither.

margin_type.description: Sport-pack vocabulary for how the margin of victory is expressed: points, goals, runs, wickets, innings_and_runs, sets, games, strokes. Blank for draws, ties and no results.

margin.description: The size of the margin in margin_type units: 3 (goals), 36 (runs), 5 (wickets), 46 (the runs part of an innings-and-46 win).

decided_by.description: How a non-regulation result was settled, sport-pack vocabulary: regulation, overtime, extra_time, penalties, shootout, super_over, golden_point, golden_set, dls, run_rule, time_limit, called_game, walkover, retired, default, awarded. Never a reason: retired and walkover carry no explanation anywhere.

neutral_site.description: true when neither team is at home; home then means first-named

toss_won_by.description: Slug of the side that won the toss or coin flip, when the sport has one.

toss_decision.description: Sport-pack vocabulary: bat, bowl (cricket); receive, defer, kick (American football); serve, receive, side (racket sports).

attendance.description: Announced attendance when the owner cares to record it

source_url.description: Box score, match report or fantasy matchup page this record was taken from

entity_types.label: Venue
entity_types.description: Where matches happen: a stadium, ground, field, park, gym or court. Teams point at their home venue; matches point at where they were held.

property_schema.description: One per physical place. A complex with several fields can be one venue with the field named on the HELD_AT edge, or one venue per field when the owner tracks them separately.

venue_type.description: What kind of place it is

surface.description: grass, turf, dirt, clay, hardwood, as the sport pack names them

entity_types.label: Stat Line
entity_types.description: A block of numbers about one subject in one context: a player's box score in a match, a team's record for a season, a player's fantasy points for a week, a career total. The stats object holds the numbers under keys the sport pack defines.

property_schema.description: Exactly one STAT_OF edge (to a person or team) and at most one RECORDED_IN edge (to the match or season it covers; career lines have none). Named <Subject> — <Context>, e.g. Jordan Lee — Week 9 2026 or Riverside Rovers — County League 2026-27. One stat_line per subject per context; update it, never create a second. Keys inside stats are lowercase snake_case from the sport pack's vocabulary and never invented.

scope.description: match: one game. segment: one innings, set, half or period inside a match, named in segment (the match line is still the one season lines sum). round: one week or matchday across games (fantasy weeks). season: aggregate over a season. career: all-time. split: a custom slice described in split_label (vs left-handers, home games, last 5).

subject_kind.description: Whether the STAT_OF target is a person or a team

stats.description: The numbers. Keys are the sport pack's stat vocabulary (e.g. passing_yards, goals, wickets, fantasy_points), lowercase snake_case, starting with a letter. Values are numbers; use null for not recorded. Durations are seconds under a key ending _seconds. Rate stats (averages, economy) are stored only when the pack lists them, otherwise the AI derives them when asked.

split_label.description: For scope split only: what the slice is

segment.description: For scope segment only: which innings, set, half or period: 1, 2, Set 3.

for_team.description: For player lines: slug of the team they were playing for in this context, when it is not obvious from the roster

games_played.description: For season, career and split scopes: how many matches the numbers cover

completeness.description: full: every key the pack lists for this scope was recorded. partial: some keys are null because nobody kept them. unknown: typed-in totals of unknown coverage. Sums skip nulls, never treat them as zero, and a season line built from any partial line is partial.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 date the numbers were last brought up to date; required for season and career lines

source.description: owner: typed in by the owner. official: from a league box score. import: from a stats site or fantasy platform. derived: computed by the AI from match lines, and so recomputable.

source_url.description: Where the numbers came from, when online

entity_types.label: Rule
entity_types.description: Standing guidance for the AI working in this world. Substance lives in lore chunks; the rule index in the world instructions says when to read each one. Sport packs ship their vocabulary as rules. Only rules with status active apply.

property_schema.description: Behaviour config in properties; prose in lore. Pause a rule by setting status paused; the data it created stays.

rule_type.description: app: a mini app that owns tags and data. workflow: a procedure. vocabulary: a sport pack's positions, stat keys, stages and values. guidance: how to behave. policy: a hard constraint. format: how to present.

trigger.description: Cue for when the AI should read this rule

scope.description: Kinds this rule reads or writes, or world for global

priority.description: Higher wins when two active rules conflict

trust.description: Provenance, highest first. Lower trust never overrides higher.

owns_tags.description: Tags this rule manages; entities carrying them are this rule's data

sport.description: For vocabulary rules: the sport code this rule defines. Blank for sport-agnostic rules.

source.description: Where the rule came from, e.g. orbismo-playbook/sports-world@1.0

relationship_types.label: Part Of
relationship_types.description: Structure. A season is part of its competition, or of a wider season (a tournament edition inside a tour year). A match or other event is part of a season and may also be part of a parent event (a tournament, a tie, a series) when it counts for both. A reserve, academy or merged team is part of its senior team.

relationship_types.label: Competes In
relationship_types.description: A team, or in individual sports a person, entered a season. Season-specific facts about the entrant live here: conference and group or division, seed, entry route, final placing, and what happened to them (promoted, relegated, withdrew).

group.description: Division, conference, group or pool label for this season: West Division, Group B, Division 2, Tuesday Co-ed

seed.description: Playoff or tournament seed once assigned

final_rank.description: Where the team finished, 1 for the champion, once the season is completed

outcome.description: What the season meant for the team; none for a mid-table finish with nothing attached

status.description: entered before play, active during, eliminated when out of a knockout, withdrawn if they left, completed when the season ends

conference.description: Conference, league half or tier the group sits in, when the competition has two levels: Conference A, East. group then holds the division alone.

entry.description: How the entrant got in, sport-pack vocabulary: direct, qualifier, wild_card, lucky_loser, protected_ranking, alternate, invited, promoted.

relationship_types.label: Plays For
relationship_types.description: A player is on a team's roster. One edge per spell at the team; set ended when they leave and start a new edge if they return. Position, number, depth, list, availability and the arrangement (contract, loan, representative, fantasy slot) live here. A team is a legal source only when a fantasy roster slot is filled by a team unit (a defence/special-teams unit): arrangement fantasy_roster, position the unit code the pack gives.

position.description: Primary position in the sport pack's vocabulary: QB, CB, GK, CM, P, SS, bat, bowl, wk

role.description: Standing on the team. captain and vice_captain are starters with the armband; practice_squad and taxi are non-active squads in American football and fantasy. injured_reserve is a reserve list that removes the player from the active roster; no reason is ever recorded.

arrangement.description: contract for pros; two_way for a contract split between a senior team and its affiliate; loan for a loanee (parent team on a second, open PLAYS_FOR edge); representative for a national, state or select side held alongside a club edge; trial for a player on trial for a contract; substitute for a one-off or occasional fill-in from outside the roster (edge opens and closes on the match date, or stays open for a regular pick-up player); amateur or volunteer for rec and club players; fantasy_roster for a fantasy team.

availability.description: Whether they can play right now. Never attach a medical reason; suspended is for disciplinary bans, and the ban's terms go in lore on the person.

slot.description: Fantasy only: the lineup slot they fill this week (QB, RB1, FLEX, BN, IR). Sport pack lists them.

acquired_via.description: How they arrived: draft, auction, keeper, trade, transfer, free_agent, waiver, academy, signup, loan, unknown

fee.description: Transfer fee or contract value as text, e.g. £45m, $2.1M/yr, undisclosed

depth_order.description: 1 for the first-string player at the position, 2 for the backup, and so on; a line or pair number in ice hockey. The pack says how it maps to labels like QB1 or WR3.

roster_list.description: Which of the team's lists the player counts against, in the pack's vocabulary: active, expanded, forty_man, practice_squad, injured_reserve, il_10, il_60, ltir, two_way, restricted, taxi. A list is a roster designation, never a reason; the reason for any unavailability is never recorded.

availability_until.description: ISO 8601 date the current availability value lapses, for suspensions and announced absences. A date only; no reason attached.

contract_until.description: Contract expiry as text: 2028-06-30, end of season, unknown.

designation.description: A roster category the league enforces, in the pack's vocabulary: designated_player, homegrown, franchise_tag, international_slot, keeper.

relationship_types.label: Staff Of
relationship_types.description: A non-playing role at a team or competition: head coach, assistant, manager, GM, owner, commissioner, trainer, analyst, scout, team parent. One edge per spell; set ended when it finishes.

role.description: manager is the soccer-style boss or the rec-team organiser; captain_organiser is the rec player who also runs the team (they get a PLAYS_FOR edge too); commissioner runs a league, so target a competition.

title.description: The exact title when the enum is too coarse: Offensive Coordinator, Bowling Coach, Director of Football

unit.description: What they coach when it matters: offense, defense, special_teams, goalkeeping, batting, bowling, fielding

relationship_types.label: Played In
relationship_types.description: A player appeared in a match (or was in the squad and did not play). One edge per player per match. Numbers go on a stat_line, not here; this edge says who was there, for which side, and in what capacity. In individual sports the COMPETED_IN edge from the person is the appearance and no PLAYED_IN edge is needed. A team source is only a fantasy team unit in a matchup.

for_team.description: Slug of the team they played for in this match, e.g. team/riverside_rovers; in a pickup game with no team entities, the side label the pack names (shirts, skins). Required whenever both sides' players link to the same event; blank only in individual sports.

started.description: true if in the starting lineup

played.description: false for an unused substitute or inactive; defaults to true

position.description: Position in this match, when it differs from the roster position

minutes.description: Minutes played, for sports that count them

entered_at.description: When a substitute came on: 67', 3rd inning, Q4

jersey_number.description: Number worn in this match if it differs from the roster number

captain.description: true if captain on the day

slot.description: Fantasy only: the lineup slot the player filled in this matchup (QB, RB, FLEX, BN, IR), from the pack's slot list. started is true for any slot that scores.

left_at.description: When the player left the field: 67', Q3, 5th inning. Blank if they finished the match.

replaced_by.description: Slug of the player who replaced this one in the match (substitute, impact player, like-for-like replacement). The reason is never recorded.

temporary.description: true when this appearance was a temporary replacement and the player it replaced later returned. The reason is never recorded.

relationship_types.label: Competed In
relationship_types.description: A team, or in individual sports a person, took part in a match. Exactly two edges per match in two-sided sports, with side saying which was home (or first-named). The score stays on the event; this edge says who and which side. On the edge to a parent tournament event it also carries that tournament's group, seed and final placing.

side.description: home or away; at a neutral site use neutral_first for the first-named team (whose score is home_score) and neutral_second for the other

result.description: This team's result, mirroring the event's result from this team's point of view, so a team's record can be read from its edges

group.description: Only on the edge to a parent tournament event: the pool or group the side was drawn into for that tournament (Pool C).

seed.description: Only on the edge to a parent tournament event: the side's seed in that tournament.

final_rank.description: Only on the edge to a parent tournament event: where the side finished in that tournament, 1 for the winner.

relationship_types.label: Officiated
relationship_types.description: A person officiated a match: referee, umpire, assistant, scorer, TMO, VAR. A team source is a work team on officiating duty at a club tournament (role work_team).

role.description: Sport-pack vocabulary: referee, assistant_referee, fourth_official, var, crew_chief, umpire, down_judge, linesman, plate_umpire, base_umpire, on_field_umpire, third_umpire, match_referee, tmo, chair_umpire, line_judge, scorer, work_team

relationship_types.label: Involved In
relationship_types.description: A person or team was part of a non-match event: drafted, traded, transferred, signed, released, honoured, present at a meeting. Which side of it they were on is the role.

role.description: subject: the person the event is about. from_team and to_team: the two clubs in a transfer or trade. drafting_team and drafted: a draft pick. traded_away and acquired: each player's direction in a trade. honoured: award recipient.

detail.description: Pick number, fee, contract length, award name, or whatever the role needs: Pick 1.07, £45m, 4 years, Top Scorer

relationship_types.label: Held At
relationship_types.description: An event took place at a venue.

field.description: Which field, pitch, court or diamond inside the venue: Field 3, Court B

relationship_types.label: Home Venue
relationship_types.description: A team's home ground. Set ended and add a new edge when a team moves.

relationship_types.label: Stat Of
relationship_types.description: Whose numbers a stat_line holds. Exactly one per stat_line.

relationship_types.label: Recorded In
relationship_types.description: The match or season a stat_line covers. At most one per stat_line; career lines have none.

relationship_types.label: Won
relationship_types.description: An honour: a team won a season or match (title, cup, final), or a person won an award tied to a season or match (most valuable player, top scorer, player of the match). The honour's name is on the edge.

title.description: Champion, Runner-up, Most Valuable Player, Top Scorer, Player of the Match, Fantasy Champion, Last Place (the trophy nobody wants)

detail.description: Vote count, record, margin or anything worth one line

relationship_types.label: Rival Of
relationship_types.description: Two teams (or two fantasy managers' teams, or two players) with a rivalry worth tracking. The story goes in lore on either side.

name.description: What the rivalry is called, if it has a name: the Derby, the Grudge Match

relationship_types.label: Applies To
relationship_types.description: A rule governs an entity. Sport-pack vocabulary rules apply to their competitions, so the AI can find the right vocabulary from any competition.
